Wymore.title: Wymore Transfer
Wymore.html:
Supporting Evidence

Ad 01.01 · 3-day trend

Metric 08.11 08.12 08.13
CTR 1.63% 1.78% 0.69%
CPC $4.50 $4.26 $11.22
Link Clicks 7 7 2
GHL Leads 0 0 0

The CTR dip is real, but even on the two good-CTR days the account produced 0 leads — so the ad is not the primary blocker. Scroll at 16% and a cumulative CR of ~5.6% point to a page that isn't holding or converting the visitors it gets.

Hypotheses (1–3)

  1. The page/handoff is the true constraint — 0 GHL leads across 3 days regardless of CTR, plus 16% scroll and ~6% CR. (high)
  2. Ad 01.01 creative is now also fatiguing (CTR <1%, CPC up) — a secondary issue. (medium)

Recommended Action

One change: fix the conversion path — start with the landing page (scroll 16%). This remains the single biggest lever: three days of spend, 0 GHL leads, and a page only 16% of visitors scroll through. Confirm the GHL tracking fires, then strengthen the above-the-fold so visitors scroll and reach the form. (The CTR-below-1% on Ad 01.01 is the next item to address once leads are flowing — but we change one thing at a time, and the page is the bigger prize.)

Expected Result

Scroll depth climbs off 16% and GHL starts recording leads from existing traffic — turning "0 leads" into a measurable CPL and CR we can then optimize.

Approval Needed

None — page/tracking work can proceed. Flag for later: Ad 01.01 creative refresh (CTR <1%).

Learning Captured

Open. Across 3 days the account's blocker is conversion, not clicks (0 GHL leads on healthy and unhealthy CTR alike). Scroll 16% is the clearest page signal yet.

Wymore.title: Wymore Transfer
Wymore.html:
Supporting Evidence

Top-of-funnel is healthy two days running (CTR ~1.7%, CPC ~$4.30). Yet GHL stays at 0 and the cumulative on-page CR (~5.8%) is far under the 25–30% target. The page is either not converting or not handing leads to GHL — and that gap, not the ad, is what's capping this account.

Hypotheses (1–3)

  1. Page→GHL tracking/handoff is broken — the most likely reason healthy click volume yields 0 recorded leads. (high)
  2. The landing page genuinely under-converts (~6% vs 25–30%). (medium)
  3. Ad 01.02 is dead weight (near-$0 spend, 0 clicks). (low)

Recommended Action

One change: verify and fix the landing-page → GHL lead tracking. Two days of healthy clicks and $0 in GHL leads is the single biggest thing holding this account back — bigger than any ad tweak. Confirm the form fires into GHL (test submission end-to-end). Until leads are trustworthy, we can't judge the page against the 25–30% target.

Expected Result

GHL begins recording leads from the traffic we're already buying, giving a real CPL and a readable page CR to act on next.

Approval Needed

None — tracking verification can proceed now.

Learning Captured

Open. Ad engagement is fine; the unresolved issue is 0 GHL leads. Confirm tracking before spending more.

Phil S (Grumpy).title: Grumpy CFO
Phil S (Grumpy).html:
Supporting Evidence

Ad 01.01 · 3-day trend

Metric 08.11 08.12 08.13
CTR 1.44% 0.69% 2.99%
CPC $6.59 $13.00 $3.91
Link Clicks 3 2 9
GHL Leads (acct) 1 1 3
Real CPL (acct) $23.41 $28.21 $13.24

Engagement is no longer the bottleneck — CTR is exceptional and CPL is under goal. What now caps results is the landing page: scroll depth is only 39%, so most visitors never reach the lower page / form. (On-page CR still untracked, so we lean on GHL + scroll.)

Hypotheses (1–3)

  1. The recovery is real and volume-driven — more qualified clicks (9) converted into 3 leads. (high)
  2. Ad 01.01 is the engine; 01.02 is marginal. (high)
  3. Low scroll (39%) is now the main drag on conversion — a stronger above-the-fold could lift leads further. (medium)

Recommended Action

One change: scale Ad 01.01's budget (modestly). It's the clear winner — CTR exceptional, CPC $3.91, CPL ~$13 under the $20 goal — so the single highest-value move is to feed more budget to it and confirm CPL holds under $20 as volume grows. (Scroll is the next lever after this, but we change one thing at a time.)

Expected Result

Higher click and lead volume from 01.01 with CPL staying at/under ~$20 — building toward the long-term 100–300 leads/month path. If CPL creeps up as we scale, that tells us where the ceiling is.

Approval Needed

Budget increase on Ad 01.01 needs your sign-off (how aggressively to scale). Everything else holds steady so the scale test is clean.

Learning Captured

First day under the short-term CPL goal ($13 vs $20). CTR recovered from the 08.12 dip to exceptional; leads 1 → 3. Next likely lever: landing-page scroll (39% vs 60%). One lead-day isn't a trend — watch 08.14.

Phil S (Grumpy).title: Grumpy CFO
Phil S (Grumpy).html:
Supporting Evidence

The leak is at ad engagement: fewer, more expensive clicks on 01.01 and nothing from 01.02. Downstream can't be judged — only 1 LP view, on-page CR still 0/untracked. The single clear, rule-triggered signal today is CTR under 1% on the main ad.

Hypotheses (1–3)

  1. Creative fatigue / weakening relevance on Ad 01.01 — CTR halved and CPM stayed high (~$89). (high)
  2. Volume starvation persists — 2 clicks can't produce measurable conversions. (medium)
  3. Tracking gap continues (on-page 0 vs GHL 1). (medium)

Recommended Action

One change: refresh the Ad 01.01 creative. Its CTR dropped below 1% — the rule's trigger to change the ad — and it's the single highest-value lever today. (Keep everything else constant so we can read the effect.)

Expected Result

Ad 01.01 CTR recovers back above 1–1.5% and CPC falls back toward ~$6, restoring click volume so leads can follow.

Approval Needed

Creative refresh can proceed without approval. Separately (not a second action): the on-page tracking gap should be fixed soon so LP CR becomes readable.

Learning Captured

Open — pending the creative refresh and 08.13 data.

Eric (Finn).title: Finn The Finnancial Guide
Eric (Finn).html:
Supporting Evidence

3-day account trend

Metric 08.11 08.12 08.13
Spend $14.66 $47.66 $47.70
Link Clicks 7 15 25
GHL Leads 2 2 9
Real CPL $7.33 $23.83 $5.30

The 08.12 "extra clicks, no leads" problem resolved itself once 02.01 found cheap, high-intent traffic (CPM halved, 19 LP views). Leads jumped to 9 at a $5.30 CPL. Engagement and cost are no longer the constraint — the page is: only 18% of visitors scroll through.

Hypotheses (1–3)

  1. Ad 02.01 unlocked efficient reach (low CPM, high CTR) that converts — the driver of the lead surge. (high)
  2. Finn is now the top-performing account; 02.01 is the engine. (high)
  3. Low scroll (18%) is leaving conversions on the table — a stronger page could lift leads further. (medium)

Recommended Action

One change: scale Ad 02.01's budget. It's a clear winner — CTR 1.81%, CPC $1.79, 9 leads at a $5.30 CPL. Feeding it more budget is the single highest-value move; watch that CPL stays low as it scales. (Improving the page's 18% scroll is the next lever after this — one change at a time.)

Expected Result

More leads per day from 02.01 with CPL holding near $5–$8 as spend rises. If CPL climbs, that marks the efficient-scale ceiling for this audience.

Approval Needed

Budget increase on Ad 02.01 needs your sign-off. Hold everything else so the scale test reads clean.

Learning Captured

Best day and best CPL of any client ($5.30, 9 leads). The 08.12 efficiency dip was a scaling-ahead-of-traffic blip, not a page failure. Next lever: page scroll (18% vs 60%).

Eric (Finn).title: Finn The Finnancial Guide
Eric (Finn).html:
Supporting Evidence

15 clicks this day vs 7 yesterday, yet the same 2 leads — the extra clicks didn't convert. That points to the click→lead step (page or tracking), not the ads: 02.02 is still engaging people well. 02.01 continues to spend inefficiently for almost no clicks.

Hypotheses (1–3)

  1. The page (or lead tracking) isn't scaling with traffic — doubling clicks added no leads. (high)
  2. Scaling 02.02's budget outpaced what the page can convert. (medium)
  3. 02.01 is a weak arm dragging efficiency (CTR <1%). (medium)

Recommended Action

One change: hold spend and investigate the click→lead drop-off (page/tracking) before scaling further. 15 clicks producing the same 2 leads is the signal to understand — pushing more budget now just raises CPL. Confirm leads are tracking and the page converts before adding spend.

Expected Result

Either we find leads that weren't being counted (CPL was actually better), or we confirm a page-conversion ceiling to fix — either way the next scale-up is on solid ground.

Approval Needed

None — this is an investigate/hold step, no budget change.

Learning Captured

Open. Efficiency dropped as 02.02 scaled (CPL $7 → $24); the extra clicks didn't convert. Understand why before spending more.

GRNDED.title: Grnded Agency
GRNDED.html:
Supporting Evidence

Ad 2.01 · 2-day trend

Metric 08.12 08.13
Spend $25.10 $43.61
CTR 2.49% 1.46%
CPC $4.18 $7.27
GHL Leads 1 4
Real CPL $25.10 $10.90

More budget produced more leads at a much better CPL — the account is scaling efficiently. The softening CTR and flat click count (6 despite +74% spend) suggest the added spend is buying pricier impressions (CPM ~$106), worth monitoring so CTR doesn't slide under 1%.

Hypotheses (1–3)

  1. Added budget reached more qualified people who converted — scaling is working. (high)
  2. CTR softened as the audience widened, but it's still healthy (1.46%). (medium)
  3. The page is relatively strong (~20% CR, near the 25–30% target). (medium)

Recommended Action

One change: continue scaling Ad 2.01's budget. It's the clear winner — leads 1 → 4, CPL down to $10.90 — so the single best move is to keep feeding it, while watching CTR (keep it above 1%) and CPC as spend grows. Hold the creative and page constant so the scale effect reads clean.

Expected Result

Continued lead growth with CPL holding around $10 or better. If CTR slides toward 1% or CPC keeps climbing as we scale, that flags the efficient-spend ceiling and the ad becomes the next thing to address.

Approval Needed

Budget increase on Ad 2.01 needs your sign-off. (Note: adding Mouseflow scroll tracking for this client would complete the picture — it's the only one without it.)

Learning Captured

Strong second day: leads 1 → 4, CPL $25 → $11, page CR ~20% (best of the group). Scaling is working; watch CTR/CPC as spend rises.
